correctness.rationale: The two-dimensional Gaussian projector moment is independently derived by an explicit polar-angle integral. Cayley-Hamilton gives \(\frac{K+\sqrt{\det K}\,I}{\operatorname{tr}K+2\sqrt{\det K}}\); substitution into \(\operatorname{tr}(A^2)-\operatorname{tr}(A^2P)\) yields the exact error. The derivative numerator factors as \((a^2-b^2)(a^2c_1-b^2c_2)\) and monotonicity of \(\sqrt{1-\rho^2}\) proves all three sharp covariance-design regimes. A nonnegative decomposition proves the if-and-only-if boundedness condition and the \(2+\tau\) crossover for every diverging singular-value ratio sequence. At both singular covariance endpoints, the one-dimensional Gaussian ray is almost surely nonzero. The independent packaged program passed 935 rational-identity, quadrature and limit checks. Finite numerical tests are not used to establish universal assertions.

value.rationale: Covariance design is central in nonstandard Gaussian randomized low-rank approximation. With the same two marginal probe variances, dependence can strictly help, hurt or have no effect, and the boundary \(a^2c_1=b^2c_2\) is complete with sharp optimizing correlations. In a high-anisotropy family, one can switch from unbounded iid-probe expected squared Frobenius error \(\kappa\) to a bounded limiting error 2 using near-perfect correlation; the precise \(\kappa^{-1}\) correlation defect window and \(2+\tau\) transition quantify the required tuning. This exact smallest nontrivial covariance optimization is a relevant finite-dimensional benchmark, not just a numerical table.
